description: Natural Language SOC (app/services/soc) inputs. The LLM is used ONLY for language understanding: it must return an app.schemas.soc_query.SOCModelIntent whose resource+operation pair is on the allowlist in app/services/soc/registry.py. It never emits SQL and never invents a table or function. The utterances below are the Gemini inputs; the structured_queries are the same intents expressed directly, so the allowlisted executor can be proven offline without an API key.

natural_language_queries.query: show me the most recent correlations
what is the risk assessment for the latest correlation?
which detections matched the suspicious PowerShell rule?
do we have any incident memory for this correlation?

structured_queries.purpose: Deterministic offline path: the validated intent is executed by the real SOCQueryExecutor without any LLM, proving the allowlisted executor can read detections.
Recent correlations feed, executed against the rows the full-SOC scenario just persisted.
Risk assessment for the correlation id the runner minted from the real pipeline; the id is substituted at run time, never hard-coded here.
Incident memories linked to a correlation, showing recalled history is retrievable next to live analytical data.
Detections for one shipped Sigma rule id, proving by_rule is allowlisted for detections. The rule id is read from the real registry at run time.

out_of_grammar_examples.query: list the files on the web server
out_of_grammar_examples.why_rejected: no allowlisted resource matches; the validator fails closed rather than guessing, and 'incident_learning' is deliberately not a resource because it has no read-only query service
the grammar is read-only: there is no write operation on the allowlist

out_of_grammar_examples.query: run SELECT against the detections table
out_of_grammar_examples.why_rejected: the model returns a structured intent only; raw SQL is never accepted or executed
